chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Keg Johnson, Al Morgan and how Milt got into Cab's band
summary: Keg went to Cab; bassist Al Morgan quit Cab in California; and Keg then recommended Milt Hinton from Chicago.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So consequently, Keg gets in there, and then he gets recommended to Cab Calloway, and Cab takes Keg out of Benny Carter's band. Teddy Wilson goes to Benny Goodman. And Al Morgan, who is from New Orleans, went to California to make a movie with Cab Calloway, The Singing Kid, and he was so photogenic out there, every time Cab looked up, the camera was on Morgan, and Cab didn't like that, and they got into little altercations. And then people told Al Morgan "If you were in California, everybody they make a picture with a Black man in it, you'd be in it." So Al Morgan quit and stayed in California; he was with Les Hite's band, see.

Then Cab was without a bass player, and he's coming back east. And Keg Johnson, it's now his turn to say, "Well, if you're coming back east, you've got to go through Chicago. Get Milt Hinton." And that's who... I was with Zutty Singleton at the Three Deuces -- with Lee Collins and Zutty Singleton. That's where I came in, through that same kind of avenue; you know, whatever the next steps were.
Well, maybe they got it today. Well, now I'm not involved with them youngsters. But I imagine it is. They know who is who, and who is on second first, and who is on and who ain't.
